sampling_model.design: Balanced fixed-rank latent-factor panel with deterministic candidate Page blocks, one common terminal block and forecast origin, and auxiliary-block empirical-risk selection with deterministic tie breaking.
sampling_model.units: One untreated target and \(N_n\) treated donors, conditioned on latent unit and time factors and assignments through lead \(H_n\).
sampling_model.treatment: Donors reveal treated post-period trajectories; the target remains untreated in the observed panel, and the target is its prospective treated conditional-mean path.
sampling_model.overlap: Unit-side and selected temporal row-span recovery hold for every candidate layout; path covariance may be singular, but each marginal leading variance is at least \(c_v^2/n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Rank-truncated PCR estimates unit and temporal coefficients; fitted Riesz vectors, the observed terminal block, recursive Jacobians, and a pooled residual variance form the observable positive-semidefinite Gram covariance.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper establishes pointwise identification, finite-sample error bounds, consistency, asymptotic normality, and inference for prespecified linear summaries over fixed forecast horizons.
The paper derives asymptotic MSPE expressions for conventional recursive and direct multistep panel-VAR forecasts and shows that their ranking changes with lag-order specification.
The paper derives asymptotic distributions and MSPE comparisons for direct and plug-in multistep predictors in finite-order autoregressive time series.
The paper obtains asymptotic MSPE expressions for plug-in and direct multistep predictors in autoregressive processes and compares their performance in stationary and deterministic-trend settings.
The procedure constructs simultaneous confidence bands for many functional parameters using approximately Neyman-orthogonal scores.
The paper gives comparison and anti-concentration bounds for maxima with arbitrary covariance matrices.
The paper derives Gaussian and bootstrap approximations uniformly over high-dimensional hyperrectangles.
The paper establishes nonasymptotic out-of-sample prediction guarantees for fixed-design principal component regression with errors in variables.
The paper establishes asymptotic normality for low-rank completion without requiring implemented sample splitting.
The paper proves residual-bootstrap intervals for individual treated unit-time effects in an interactive-fixed-effects panel.
The paper derives expected-width lower bounds for honest random confidence bands over nonparametric regression classes.

body.tldr: A selected-training Two-Way Synthetic Forecasting path is treated as one growing, conditionally Gaussian orthogonal-score object rather than as a collection of pointwise forecasts. On a balanced strongly identified fixed-rank panel class, the paper derives the joint direct and recursive scores, constructs observable positive-semidefinite Gram covariance estimators from the fitted PCR, Riesz, terminal-block, and recursive-Jacobian objects, and proves feasible multiplier coverage for \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\). The covariance decomposition yields a heterogeneous variance-share frontier: recursive Gaussian complexity is uniformly bounded, whereas direct complexity is comparable to \(1+\rho_n\), the expected maximum of independent normals scaled by their lead-specific direct shares. This complexity and simultaneous-inference comparison is distinct from the direct-versus-recursive panel-VAR MSPE ranking of Greenaway-McGrevy (2013). A persistent rank-one subclass gives the exact limits \(\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}\to\sqrt{2/\pi}\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n}/\sqrt{\log H_n}\to1\); a separate explicit rank-two TWSF Gaussian-location submodel yields probability and expected maximum-width lower bounds for uniformly honest rectangles centered at the direct leading Gaussian estimator. An \(H_n=1\) singleton-menu inclusion recovers Shen's pointwise setup solely as prior-art validation.

project_justification.gap: Shen (2026, Corollary 2 and Section 6) establishes pointwise inference for prespecified fixed-horizon summaries, not a growing selected path. Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) derives asymptotic MSPE expressions for conventional direct and recursive panel-VAR forecasts, but an MSPE ranking does not provide a causal TWSF selected-training score, a Gaussian maximum or variance-share frontier, a feasible cross-lead Gram covariance, or a simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon. Generic orthogonal-score and Gaussian-comparison results begin after uniform linearization and covariance control have been supplied.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is an observable joint law for direct and recursive causal conditional-mean paths that remains valid under singular correlation and exposes how a heterogeneous vector of lead-specific innovations alters the critical-value scale, a criterion orthogonal to forecast MSPE ranking.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the stacked causal TWSF score and positive-semidefinite Gram map, proves the actual-estimator relative covariance and simultaneous-coverage rates at \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\), characterizes direct complexity through the aggregate heterogeneous-share quantity \(\rho_n\), and certifies the architectural separation on a persistent rank-one subclass. It places the centered-rectangle width cost on an explicit legal rank-two Gaussian-location submodel and embeds Shen's published pointwise setup at \(H_n=1\) with singleton training menus; it makes no claim to sharpen Greenaway-McGrevy's panel-VAR MSPE ranking.

body.related_work: Shen (2026) is the exact causal-forecasting anchor: Theorem 1 identifies the prospective treated conditional mean, Corollary 2 gives pointwise inference, and Section 6 treats prespecified direct and recursive summaries over fixed horizons. The explicit \(H_n=1\) singleton-menu inclusion recovers that pointwise interval as a validation check, not as novelty; the selected growing-path theorem strictly tightens the published fixed-summary result by covering all \(H_n\) conditional means jointly. Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) is the nearest direct-versus-recursive architecture comparator in panel forecasting: the paper derives asymptotic MSPE expressions for conventional recursive, or plug-in, and direct multistep forecasts in a panel vector autoregression, with the ranking governed by lag-order specification. That MSPE comparison informs the architectural motivation but does not supply the causal TWSF selected-training score construction, Gaussian maximum or variance-share complexity frontier, feasible Gram covariance, or simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon. Bhansali (1997) provides the earlier time-series comparison of direct and plug-in autoregressive predictors through asymptotic distributions, MSPE, and efficiency loss, not a panel causal path law. Ing (2003) likewise compares plug-in and direct multistep predictors by asymptotic MSPE in autoregressive processes, including deterministic-trend cases, without addressing selected low-rank panel inference. Belloni, Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Wei (2018) inform the use of uniform orthogonal expansions and multiplier critical values but do not derive the low-rank panel scores. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015, 2017) inform comparison, anti-concentration, and singular-covariance hyperrectangle approximation; they are probability inputs rather than theorem-level targets. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025) inform the fixed-design PCR perturbation step, while Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024) inform the proof-only decoupling of factor estimation from target noise. Li, Shen, and Zhou (2024) provide the nearest residual-bootstrap panel inference, but their object is an individual treated unit-time effect rather than a prospective growing path. Cai, Low, and Ma (2014) inform random-band width arguments; the present lower result is confined to rectangles centered at the direct leading Gaussian estimator in the explicit legal family \(\mathcal L_n\).
body.technical_internal_limitation: The first kill test is the actual-estimator three-piece perturbation \(\widehat q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}-q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=(\widehat Z^\dagger-\bar Z^\dagger)J_{n,\ell}^{\top}w_n+\widehat Z^\dagger J_{n,\ell}^{\top}(W_n^{\top}\widehat\beta_n-w_n)+\widehat Z^\dagger(\widehat J_{n,\ell}-J_{n,\ell})^{\top}W_n^{\top}\widehat\beta_n\). The proposal fails if an independent audit finds an order-one studentized term, an invalid projector-response independence step, or a need to replace observed \(W_n\) or fitted \(J_{n,\ell}\) by oracle objects. The rank-two location construction also requires a cell-index audit showing that the constant and alternating factors realize every displayed block with disjoint cells and a power-bounded two-root recurrence. Explicit constants, measurable exceptional-event endpoints, finite multiplier-simulation error, and software integration remain proof and implementation tasks rather than additional assumptions.
body.honest_scope: The proved target is the prospective treated conditional-mean path, not realized-future prediction. Training-layout selection must use the declared auxiliary block; arbitrary reuse of inference cells and data-driven selection between direct and recursive modes are excluded. The result assumes independent homoskedastic Gaussian cell errors, fixed rank, strong spectral identification, and the sufficient growing horizon \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\). The exact recursive and direct complexity limits hold on the persistent all-ones subclass, while the heterogeneous-share order comparison holds over \(\mathcal C_n\); a minimum-share-only upper law is asserted only under uniform share comparability. The width lower bound uses the nondegenerate legal rank-two family \(\mathcal L_n\), concerns rectangles centered at its direct leading Gaussian estimator, and makes no unrestricted-estimator minimax claim. The \(H_n=1\) singleton-menu result is only a prior-art reduction. The sharp maximal growing horizon is left as the explicit open-ended question.
